text.title: AI LLM Workload Architecture Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Does the change touch an LLM call path — prompt text, system prompt, model id, sampling parameters, retrieval configuration, or tool schemas?

branch.conclusion: Skip. No LLM behaviour can regress from this change; ordinary code review and tests apply.

branch.question: Is there a version-pinned eval set (git ref or content hash recorded as `eval_set_ref`) with a baseline run URL in `evidence[]`?

branch.conclusion: Stop. Build or pin the eval set, run the current commit as the baseline, record its URL, then re-enter the tree.

branch.question: Does the scoring function give the same score on re-run at the same commit, and is the eval suite a merge-blocking CI job with numeric per-metric thresholds?

branch.conclusion: Pin the judge model id, temperature 0, and judge prompt hash (or switch to exact-match / schema scoring); re-run twice to establish the noise floor before setting thresholds.
Wire the eval suite as a required CI check on prompt, model, retrieval and tool-schema paths; set thresholds against the baseline; only then merge the change.
Run the full procedure: pinned model id, latency and cost budgets, injection cases and the degradation path all present in the spec; emit the artefact per the output contract.

example.p: PR rewrites the system prompt of the ticket summariser: touches the LLM path. Eval set is pinned at `evals/summariser@a1b2c3d` with a baseline run linked. The judge is `claude` on an alias with temperature 0.7: scoring is not deterministic → conclusion r-scoring-function-deterministic; the PR waits until the judge is pinned and the baseline re-run.
